Title: Police hunt woman who kicked auxiliary policeman in groin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are tracking down a woman who kicked an auxiliary policeman in the groin after he confronted her for driving against traffic flow near a shopping complex in Damansara yesterday.
Police have identified the suspect and believed that she could be on the run.
Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said the incident occurred at 8.38am while the 30-year-old auxiliary policeman was on duty.
He said the policeman noticed a Hyundai Inokom parked facing the wrong direction, with its driver honking at other vehicles without reason.
The officer approached the woman and advised her to move the vehicle.
"However, the suspect showed an obscene gesture," Hoo said when contacted.
He said the woman then got out of the vehicle and attempted to attack the policeman before kicking him in the groin.
The policeman sought help from other personnel as he struggled with the woman and tried to restrain her, but she managed to flee.
"Efforts to track down the suspect are ongoing," Hoo said.
The case is being investigated under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955 for insulting behaviour.

Title: Malaysians in Istanbul safe amid flash floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: No Malaysians are affected by floods in Istanbul, Turkiye, following unusually heavy rain and strong winds since late Tuesday night.
Malaysian Consul in Istanbul Mardhiah Sabri said the consulate was closely monitoring the situation to ensure Malaysians' safety in the city.
"As of noon local time, no Malaysians have been reported seriously affected. The consulate is also keeping close contact with Malaysian community representatives and student associations to ensure prompt consular assistance if needed.
"Safety advisories have also been issued through the consulate's official channels," she told Buletin TV3.
She said heavy rain since Oct 13 had flooded several parts of Istanbul, affecting roads and residential areas.
Among the worst-hit areas were Beykoz, Sarıyer and Eyüpsultan, which recorded the highest rainfall, as well as Esenyurt and Kağıthane.
"According to the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality's Disaster Coordination Centre (AKOM), rainfall in several districts exceeded 240mm, while wind speeds were forecast to reach between 50 and 80 kilometres per hour.
"However, public transport services have shown signs of recovery, with most closed roads reopened and affected metro and tram services returning to normal.
"Nevertheless, several ferry routes remain cancelled or have been diverted, while a temporary ban has been imposed on motorcycles on city roads," she said.
Mardhiah advised Malaysians in Istanbul, as well as those planning to travel to the city, to follow local authorities' instructions on safety advisories issued through the consulate's official channels.
They were also told to stay away from flooded areas, underpasses and basements, and not to attempt to cross flooded roads.
"Malaysians scheduled to depart for Istanbul are advised to check their flight status with their respective airlines before heading to the airport.
"The Consulate General of Malaysia in Istanbul will continue to monitor developments in coordination with the Turkish authorities and provide Malaysians with the latest updates," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze forces postponement of UASA next week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry has postponed the Academic Year-End Assessment (UASA), scheduled for next week, due to the haze affecting the country.
In a statement today, the ministry said the decision was made after taking into account concerns raised by parents and guardians over their children's health, particularly those who would need to attend school to sit for the assessment.
"As UASA is a school-based assessment, schools have been given the flexibility to reschedule it.
"The revised schedule will be communicated to parents and guardians by their respective schools at a later date," the statement said.
The ministry acknowledged the dilemma faced by parents who wanted to protect their children's health but were also concerned that their absence from school could result in them missing an important assessment.
It said the health and safety of students would remain its priority while ensuring that all assessment processes were carried out in an orderly manner.

Title: Ministry studies OTP to curb abandoned projects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry is studying a proposed option-to-purchase (OTP) mechanism to reduce sick and abandoned housing projects and better protect homebuyers.
Its minister Nga Kor Ming said the mechanism would introduce a more structured process before sale and purchase agreements are signed, allowing developers to gauge genuine demand while safeguarding buyers' interests.
"At present, developers often assess market demand through the collection of booking fees.
"However, this presents several challenges, including difficulties in distinguishing genuine buyers from those who are not serious about purchasing, while homebuyers risk losing their booking fees if they choose not to proceed," he said.
Under the proposed mechanism, developers would be given a specified period to assess buyer interest before deciding whether to proceed.
Buyers could pay up to five per cent of the proposed purchase price and submit their financial information for loan assessments.
If the developer decides not to proceed, buyers would receive a full refund together with accrued interest.
Through the proposed OTP mechanism, developers would be required to honour the indicative price initially offered to buyers, ensuring that the final selling price remains unchanged.
"For developers, this means greater certainty over genuine market demand. For homebuyers, it means greater transparency and price certainty before making a major financial commitment.
"Through this reform, we want to ensure that buyers will never have to pay for houses that they will never get," he said at the 5th Malaysia Developer Awards 2026 on Wednesday.
Meanwhile, Nga said the ministry secured a larger allocation under the 2027 Budget to implement big data analytics to address housing supply-demand mismatches.
This follows an 8.6 per cent increase in completed but unsold residential units in the first half of 2026.
The initiative would also support the government's target of delivering one million affordable homes over the next decade under the National Housing Policy 2026–2035.

Title: Private hospitals expect faster licensing with e-CKAPS portal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Private hospitals expect less paperwork, shorter approval times and greater certainty for operators with the introduction of a fully digitalised licensing system under the 2027 Budget.
Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM) president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh said the e-CKAPS portal would streamline the licensing process for private healthcare facilities, which has traditionally relied on manual procedures.
"At the Budget dialogue, we made the case that technology benefits both public and private healthcare by making our processes more efficient.
"Licensing is one of the most process heavy areas for private hospitals, and our licensing process has been a manual process.
"With a fully digitalised system, we expect to see a significant reduction in paperwork, shorter approval times, and greater certainty for operators," he said in a statement.
The government has allocated RM7.5 million under the 2027 Budget to develop the e-CKAPS portal, which is expected to
reduce licensing processing
times by up to 65 per cent.
Kuljit said the portal could set a benchmark for wider digitalisation across the healthcare sector, in line with Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad's vision for a digitalised healthcare system.
It added that its inclusion in the Budget shows the government's willingness to listen to industry and to act on practical reforms that improve how healthcare is regulated and delivered.
"APHM sees this as an important step towards a more connected and efficient national healthcare system. APHM looks forward to working closely with the ministry on the design and rollout of e-CKAPS," he said.

Title: Another brazen cable theft caught on video, cops hunt 5 men in Johor
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police are hunting five men caught on video stealing cables in Taman Melodies here, after the footage went viral on social media.
Johor Baru (South) police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said the video showed the men cutting cables and loading them into a car.
He said an internal police report was lodged at 4.16pm yesterday after a senior police officer came across a social media post uploaded at 2.20pm the same day.
"Police identified the vehicle owner through its registration number, and efforts to identify and track down all five suspects are ongoing," he said in a statement.
The case is being investigated under Section 379 of the Penal Code for theft, which carries a jail term of up to seven years, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Those with information on the incident can contact the Johor Baru South district police headquarters or its hotline at 07-2182323.
On Tuesday, it was reported that a cable theft gang suspected of operating in four states had been busted after members were filmed stealing Telekom Malaysia cables in broad daylight using a Mercedes-Benz and a pickup truck.
Fourteen people, including two women, were arrested following a viral video showing the suspects in action near a primary school in Kampung Melayu Panchor on Oct 9.
The suspects, aged between 22 and 67, were arrested in a series of raids in Labu, Nilai and Dengkil, Selangor.

Title: CelcomDigi pays RM382mil for spectrum bands
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CelcomDigi Bhd has paid RM381.75 million for spectrum assignments in the 2600MHz and 900MHz frequency bands to strengthen network capacity and coverage.
Its unit, CelcomDigi Telecommunications Sdn Bhd (CDTel), made the full payment today after accepting the terms and conditions in the notice of award issued by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
The award covers 2x20MHz in the 2600MHz band for four years and 2x5MHz in the 900MHz band for five years.
The notice followed the issuance of an Application Information Package on Aug 14.
CelcomDigi said the additional spectrum would improve capital expenditure efficiency while enhancing network capacity and service quality to meet growing customer demand.
"The assignment enables a contiguous 2x40MHz spectrum holding in the 2600MHz spectrum frequency band and improves the company's spectrum position in the 900MHz spectrum frequency band to support wider and deeper coverage across the country," it said in a statement.
The additional 2600MHz spectrum will expand CelcomDigi's contiguous spectrum holding in the band, while the 900MHz allocation is expected to strengthen coverage across the country.
CelcomDigi shares closed six sen, or 2.39 per cent, higher at RM2.57 today, giving the telecommunications group a market capitalisation of RM30.15 billion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GWM adds two outlets as deliveries rise
Article:
GWM Malaysia has added two dealerships in Johor and Selangor as vehicle deliveries rose 33 per cent year-on-year to 5,165 units in the first nine months of 2026.
The new outlets, GWM Skudai in Johor Bahru and GWM Equine Park in Seri Kembangan, bring the brand's nationwide network to more than 40 outlets covering its Haval, Tank, Ora and Wey marques.
GWM Skudai, operated by Auto Elegance Sdn Bhd, officially opened on Oct 8.
The 22,006 sq ft facility combines sales, service and spare parts operations, with three service bays and capacity to service about 150 vehicles a month.
It also has five vehicle display spaces, an electric vehicle charging station, diagnostic equipment and a dedicated vehicle delivery bay.
The outlet supports about 40 jobs across sales, technical, service and customer support functions.
Customers can view and test-drive selected models including the Haval H6, Wey G9, Tank 300, Tank 500 and Ora Good Cat.
Auto Elegance managing director Yang Ce said the company saw potential for the brand in Johor and wanted to build long-term relationships with local customers.
"We are proud to expand our partnership with GWM into Johor Bahru," he said, adding that the outlet aimed to provide customers with support from vehicle purchase through ownership.
GWM Equine Park, operated by Golden Admiral Motors Sdn Bhd, was officially opened on Oct 10, although its showroom began operations in April and its service centre opened in August.
The outlet serves customers in Seri Kembangan, Putrajaya, Cyberjaya and surrounding areas. Its showroom and service centre occupy separate premises with a combined built-up area of about 9,431 sq ft.
The showroom can accommodate at least seven vehicles, while the 3,661 sq ft service centre has four vehicle hoists, wheel-alignment and tyre-balancing equipment, and diagnostic facilities for internal combustion engine, hybrid, plug-in hybrid and electric vehicles.
Golden Admiral Motors managing director Datuk William Chang Yoong Hsi said the company had invested in facilities, equipment and staff to support customers over the longer term.
"Our goal is that every customer should feel welcomed, listened to and properly supported from the first vehicle enquiry and test drive to vehicle delivery, scheduled servicing and long-term ownership," he said.
GWM Malaysia managing director Stan Li Hao said network growth needed to be matched by consistent service standards.
"Our priority is not simply to add more locations, but to make our products and services more accessible while delivering a consistent experience at every customer touchpoint," he said.
Chief operating officer Roslan Abdullah said the company was also strengthening technical training, parts availability and dealer operating standards as its range expands across different powertrain technologies.
"A strong ownership experience depends on what happens after the vehicle leaves the showroom," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Schools in eight Selangor districts to close tomorrow
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Schools in eight districts in Selangor will be closed tomorrow due to the haze.
The Selangor Education Department said the closure would affect schools under the Klang, Kuala Selangor, Kuala Langat, Hulu Langat, Gombak, Sepang, Petaling Perdana and Petaling Utama district education offices.
Schools under the Hulu Selangor and Sabak Bernam district education offices will operate as usual.
However, all outdoor activities in the two districts are prohibited.
"Parents, guardians, students and the wider education community are advised to take note of this announcement and refer to the department's channels for the latest updates," it said in a statement.
Meanwhile, in PENANG, the Penang State Education Department (JPNPP) announced that all educational institutions under its purview will also operate as usual tomorrow, but all outdoor classroom activities must be postponed.
"As of 2 pm, Oct 15, API readings at all monitoring stations in the state were recorded below the 150 level. Pupils attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a health protection measure," it said in a statement.
The statement also noted that parents or guardians concerned about their children's health following the haze situation may consider keeping them home, provided they notify the school authorities.

Title: Malaysian arrested in Singapore with more than 700 cigarette cartons hidden in car panels
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Behind the car radio, inside door panels and beneath the boot lining, almost every hollow space in a Malaysia-registered car was used to conceal contraband cigarettes bound for Singapore.
The elaborate concealment failed at Woodlands Checkpoint on Oct 5, when Singapore's Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) officers stopped the vehicle for enhanced checks.
They uncovered more than 700 cartons and 2,000 packets of duty-unpaid cigarettes.
The 32-year-old Malaysian driver was arrested, and both him and the seized cigarettes were referred to Singapore Customs.
Despite Singapore's tough stance on contraband, cigarette smuggling attempts persist, driven by the lucrative black market.
The seizure highlights persistent cigarette smuggling attempts despite Singapore's tough stance on contraband, with high tobacco taxes creating a lucrative market for illicit cigarettes.
As a price benchmark, cartons of 10 packets of premium cigarettes in Singapore can retail for S$160 (about RM509).
At that price, 700 cartons and another 2,000 packets would have a hypothetical legal retail value of about S$144,000 (RM458,000). However, the actual value would depend on the brands involved, their purchase costs and the prices charged on the illegal market.
The latest interception follows a similar case in August, when ICA officers at Woodlands Checkpoint found more than
700 cartons
and over 100 packets of duty-unpaid cigarettes hidden in modified compartments of another Malaysia-registered car.
The repeated attempts come despite stiff penalties for cigarette smuggling in Singapore.
Under the Customs Act and Goods and Services Tax Act, offenders dealing in duty-unpaid cigarettes can face fines of up to 40 times the duty and GST evaded, imprisonment of up to six years, or both.
Vehicles used in such offences and proceeds from the illegal trade may also be forfeited.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: M'sian man held at Kualanamu Airport with syabu hidden in folded banknotes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 39-year-old man from Negri Sembilan was arrested by Indonesian Customs officers after arriving at Kualanamu International Airport in North Sumatra at 8am today.
The suspect arrived on an AirAsia flight from Kuala Lumpur, according to Indonesian news portal Analisadaily.com.
An unidentified Kualanamu Customs officer said the man was detained after authorities became suspicious during routine checks on his person and belongings at the international arrivals terminal.
"During a manual inspection, officers found powdered syabu hidden in the folds of banknotes kept in the suspect's trouser pocket," the officer was quoted as saying.
The report said the suspect was subjected to a thorough inspection after authorities found that he had frequently travelled to Indonesia, raising their suspicions.
Following his arrest, the suspect and the suspected 1.5g consignment of syabu were handed over to the Deli Serdang Police Narcotics Investigation Unit for further investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia has no plans for legal action or diplomatic note to Indonesia over haze
Article:
REMBAU: Malaysia has no plans to send a diplomatic note or take legal action against Indonesia over the transboundary haze currently affecting the country, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said such action was unnecessary as it could affect the good relations between the two countries.
"We have not reached that stage (of sending a diplomatic note). It is easy to say so in parliament, but if we were to do that, it would mean we were prepared to sever diplomatic ties.
"We need to safeguard the close relationship between the two countries. So, we are not going as far as sending a diplomatic note or taking legal action," he told reporters at Dewan Orang Ramai Rantau.
He was responding to a call by Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman for the government to take action against Indonesia, including lodging a diplomatic protest over open burning in the country that has contributed to the haze.
Syed Saddiq was reported to have said the government should not rely solely on meetings with Indonesian leaders, but should issue a clear diplomatic note with the support of other affected Asean countries, particularly Singapore.
Mohamad, who is also Rembau MP, said sending a diplomatic note was not the best way forward, as Malaysia had to take its relationship with Indonesia into account.
He said such a move might be a last resort, adding that Malaysia was currently opting for discussions and diplomacy to address the issue.
"A more appropriate approach is through diplomacy, which is the best way forward rather than sending a diplomatic note.
"I have discussed this with my counterpart, while the prime minister and deputy prime minister have also contacted the Indonesian president to discuss the matter," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Genting Plantations, Huawei team up on 174ha Johor tech campus
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Plantations Bhd's property arm has partnered with Huawei Technologies (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd to masterplan a 174-hectare smart campus in Johor, marking the Chinese technology group's first international smart campus partnership.
Genting Property Sdn Bhd signed a master planning agreement with Huawei to advance the Johor Tech Smart City (JTSC) development, including its flagship Smart Campus within the Knowledge AI Campus.
The agreement was formalised at the Shenzhen Longgang International Art Centre in China, alongside Huawei's "Cloud-Powered Infrastructure – A New Digital Ecosystem" event.
The partnership will bring Huawei's artificial intelligence capabilities, technological expertise and smart campus experience into the development's planning phase, drawing on its existing smart campus projects in Shanghai and Dongguan.
Genting Plantations chief executive and executive director Datuk Indera Lim Keong Hui said the collaboration would help translate the development's vision into tangible economic opportunities.
"This partnership answers a vital question we asked ourselves when designing JTSC: How do we build the future today to make a profound, real-world impact?" he said.
He added that the project would empower local talent and attract sought-after investments, positioning Malaysians to benefit from technological growth at home.
Huawei Malaysia deputy chief executive of its Enterprise Business Group, Du Xianjun, said the partnership marked the first time the company's smart campus model would be extended to an international partner.
"The 174ha Smart Campus in JTSC will serve as a benchmark model for how future intelligent ecosystems are built and managed worldwide," he said.
Beyond the campus, the collaboration could extend to digital transformation across the wider Genting Plantations group, including agricultural technology, sustainable energy management and data-driven corporate infrastructure.
The development is also intended to support the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone by attracting multinational technology companies, advanced manufacturing investments and innovation-driven businesses.
The signing was witnessed by Genting Bhd executive chairman Tan Sri Lim Kok Thay and Huawei executive member of the supervisory board and chief logistics officer Ren Shulu.

Title: Bollywood actor Imran Khan asked to leave India after participating in protest
Article:
MUMBAI: Indian authorities have asked Bollywood actor Imran Khan to leave the country by the end of the month, saying he breached immigration laws after joining a protest against the election commission chief, local media reported on Thursday.
Khan, 43, is a US citizen, the Indian Express newspaper reported. Under Indian law, foreigners' participation in political protests may be treated as a violation of immigration and visa rules.
Khan was given until October 28 to leave the country, the Times of India newspaper said
The actor participated in a rally in Mumbai on October 10, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over voter list revisions that critics and opposition parties say favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party
"Apparently I'm going for a drive," the actor wrote on his Instagram on the same day, with a picture of him posing with a victory sign in the back of what looked like a police van
A complaint was filed against him at a police station in Mumbai, saying Khan had breached the law, and the Foreigners Regional Registration Office, a federal government agency responsible for tracking and monitoring foreign nationals in India, sent him a notice to leave based on the complaint, the Indian Express said
Khan did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters
A nephew of actor Aamir Khan, and hailing from an illustrious film family, Imran acted in several hit Bollywood films from 2008 to 2015, before suddenly retiring. — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Anwar Ibrahim: A Life Recorded' book to be launched in March
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A book titled Anwar Ibrahim: A Life Recorded (Anwar Ibrahim: Kisah yang Dirakam), chronicling the life, struggles and leadership journey of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, will be launched in March next year.
Published by the Malaysian Care and Concern for Humanity Organisation (Malaysia Peduli) in Bahasa Melayu and English, the book features photographs, archival materials, documents and historical records relating to the Prime Minister.
The pre-launch ceremony for the coffee table book was officiated by the Finance Minister's political secretary, Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim, here today. Also present was Malaysia Peduli chairman Noor Sham @ Ann Abu Samah.
Speaking to reporters, Muhammad Kamil said the book was important in helping younger generations understand the Prime Minister's life journey.
"I think it is very important, particularly for the younger generation, to understand the history of the Prime Minister's struggles and journey.
"These experiences have been documented in a book so that it can serve as a guide and lesson, and perhaps also as a source of reflection for society," he said.
The book traces key moments that have shaped the Prime Minister's journey, from his early years and the ideals underpinning his struggles through various challenges and changes, to his responsibilities as the country's leader and Malaysia's role on the international stage.
The publication brings together a visual record of a journey intertwined with Malaysia's social, political and historical developments.
The book was made possible through the support and cooperation of various parties, which provided guidance, access to resources, expertise and other assistance, including the National Archives of Malaysia and the Information Department of Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Activist, 2 others nabbed over temple statue vandalism
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Three people, including an activist, were remanded for three days to assist in investigations into the vandalism of four statues at a temple in Jalan Klang Lama on Oct 6.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the trio were arrested in Beranang, Selangor, on Oct 11 and released on police bail on Tuesday.
"Initial investigations found that four religious statues at the temple had been damaged. However, the value of the losses has yet to be established," he said in a statement.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 295 of the Penal Code.
Fadil added that the investigation papers had been referred to the Selangor State Prosecution Office for further action.
Earlier, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan had urged police to investigate after a video of the vandalism went viral.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Court upholds 30-year sentence for man who killed stepbrother, concealed body
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today upheld a 30-year jail sentence and 12 strokes of the rotan imposed on a former trader for murdering his step-brother and concealing his body in a cement-filled drum.
A three-judge panel comprising Judges Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar unanimously dismissed Mohamad Zamhuri Azami's appeal against his conviction and sentence.
The panel also dismissed the prosecution's appeal to impose the death penalty on the 31-year-old accused.
Delivering the court's unanimous decision, Noorin said the sentence imposed by the High Court was appropriate and did not warrant appellate intervention.
"We also find no sufficient grounds to replace the sentence with the death penalty or a 40-year prison term, as requested by the prosecution," she said.
Noorin said the possibility of an argument or altercation between the appellant and the deceased did not, in itself, establish that the fatal act was justified under the defence of private defence.
She also said the prosecution had successfully established the necessary intention through the evidence presented, leaving no grounds to substitute the conviction with one under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
On May 13 last year, the Alor Star High Court found Zamhuri guilty of murdering Mohd Hasnul Nizar Khairul Anuar, 34, and sentenced him to 30 years in prison and 12 strokes of the cane.
The offence was committed at their home in Kampung Padang Hassan, Bukit Pinang, Alor Setar, Kedah, at 7.15 pm on March 6, 2020.
According to the facts of the case, the appellant led police to the location where the victim's body was concealed in a blue plastic drum filled with cement outside the house. Police also seized a meat-cleaving knife.
During today's proceedings, defence counsel Ai Cha Ran argued that his client had not intended to kill his step-brother, claiming that the deceased had attacked him during an altercation and that he had acted in self-defence.
He further submitted that the evidence supported only a charge of culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code.
However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Aqilah Syaza Ariffin argued that the pathologist's testimony showed that the victim's injuries, particularly a long and deep incised wound to the neck, were inconsistent with the defence's account of a fight or struggle.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: When accident is off-duty but the financial pain isn't [WATCH]
Article:
FOR most workers, a workplace accident is easy enough to picture: a fall at a construction site, an injury involving machinery, a collision while making a delivery. But some accidents happen nowhere near the workplace and can still follow a worker straight back to it.
A fall down the stairs at home, an injury on a hiking trail or even a cat bite may have nothing to do with the job, yet any of them can leave a worker unable to work, with an empty chair at the workplace and a household suddenly having to cope without its usual income.
That's the gap Malaysia's LINDUNG 24 Jam scheme is designed to address: what happens when an accident unrelated to a person's job leaves them temporarily unable to work.
In its first three months, PERKESO recorded 6,330 claims under the scheme, with RM9.97 million in benefits paid out.
Because when a worker cannot work, the distinction between where an accident happened and where its consequences are felt can become rather academic.
AN ORDINARY DAY GOES WRONG
[[nid:1556298]]
Some of the cases highlighted by PERKESO show just how far removed an accident can be from the conventional idea of workplace risk: a young worker in Sabah who fell down a staircase at home, another injured while hiking and a veterinary assistant seriously hurt by a cat bite. Other claims involved road accidents and incidents during workers' personal time.
Yet the common thread wasn't where the accident happened, but what followed: a worker suddenly unable to do the job that provides an income.
The first three months of claims also point to who may have the least room to absorb such a disruption: workers earning below RM3,500 accounted for 74 per cent of all claims, according to PERKESO.
Edmund Cheong Peck Huang, PERKESO's deputy chief executive (Strategy and Corporate Social Security Organisation), said the high proportion highlighted the financial vulnerability of lower-income workers when an accident takes them out of the workforce.
"For a lower-income worker, being unable to work for even two or three months due to an injury isn't just a temporary inconvenience. It immediately threatens family survival."
In July alone, applications rose to 2,135 from 616 in June, while RM3.45 million in benefits was paid to 2,508 recipients. More than 90 per cent of claims were processed and approved within five days.
Rent still has to be paid, children still need to get to school, groceries still have to be bought and loan repayments continue to fall due.
THE RISK WE DON'T SEE
[[nid:1556297]]
The numbers also reveal a more complicated picture.
As of September, 8.5 million workers, or 87.6 per cent, remained enrolled in LINDUNG 24 Jam, while about 1.2 million, or 12.4 per cent, had opted out. Of those who left, 52 per cent earned below RM3,500.
The figures alone don't explain why individual workers chose to opt out, and income cannot be assumed to be the reason. But PERKESO said it has identified an awareness and
perception gap around the scheme.
For some workers, Cheong said, the monthly contribution can feel like another deduction from their pay rather than protection against a risk they may never have to face.
Then there's the familiar thought: it won't happen to me.
For workers who are healthy and active, an off-work accident can seem like a distant possibility - until it isn't. Some also continue to associate PERKESO protection mainly with accidents at the workplace or while commuting, and may not realise that LINDUNG 24 Jam extends to qualifying accidents outside working hours and unrelated to employment.
Others, he added, believe the claims process is complicated, rigid or slow. The challenge, ultimately, is a familiar one: getting people to think about the risk while it's still only a possibility, rather than after it has become a problem.
WHAT THE CLAIMS REVEALED
The first three months have also given PERKESO a clearer picture of the risks workers face outside the workplace. Cheong said what stood out was the "sheer volume and everyday nature" of hazards that had previously been less visible within the social security framework.
Claims have involved routine domestic and recreational activities, including falls from ladders during home renovations, serious cat bites, weekend sports injuries and road accidents during personal travel.
The overall volume rose sharply, from an average of about 16 claims a day in June to roughly 69 a day by August — more than four times higher. The experience reinforced PERKESO's view that risks don't stop when workers clock out.
Formal-sector workers spend roughly 33 per cent of their time working, including commuting, meaning about 67 per cent of their time is spent outside working hours.
The point isn't that every minute outside work carries the same level of risk. It's that a worker remains a worker — with bills, dependants and earning responsibilities — even when an accident occurs somewhere that has nothing to do with the job.
WHEN WORKERS RETURN
By September, about 10,000 workers who'd previously opted out had returned to LINDUNG 24 Jam. Cheong said PERKESO had found that greater awareness of risk was a key reason workers returned to the scheme.
He pointed to cases in which workers had opted out and subsequently suffered non-work injuries, only to find they weren't eligible for LINDUNG 24 Jam benefits because they were no longer participating.
Such cases, he said, had served as "eye-openers" within communities.
The increase in reported claims, together with a simplified online re-entry process, also gave workers a way to reconsider their decision.
It's difficult to know what prompted each individual worker to return. But the broader pattern is revealing: protection that can feel unnecessary when nothing has happened can look rather different after something does.
SAFETY NET WITH LIMITS
LINDUNG 24 Jam isn't intended to cover every illness or situation. It applies to eligible employees for qualifying accidents occurring outside working hours and unrelated to employment, subject to the applicable conditions.
Participation for local employees is voluntary, with the worker bearing the contribution. The contribution rate is implemented in phases, starting at 0.75 per cent, rising to 1 per cent for years three to five and 1.25 per cent from the sixth year onwards.
Cheong said another misconception PERKESO encounters is the idea that social security works like an individual savings account, with contributions accumulating for personal withdrawal. Instead, he explained, PERKESO operates on the principle of social solidarity and risk pooling, with contributions supporting a collective social security system.
In other words, the scheme isn't a promise that nothing will go wrong. It's an attempt to provide protection for what happens when something does.
ACCIDENTS AND CONSEQUENCES
[[nid:1556296]]
A staircase at home may have nothing to do with a person's occupation, just as a hiking trail or a road outside working hours may have nothing to do with the job listed on a payslip.
But if an injury means that person cannot stand behind a counter, operate machinery, drive a vehicle, lift goods, work a shift or simply turn up for work, the boundary between a private accident and a workplace problem becomes considerably less clear.
The workplace is where a person earns a living, but it's only one part of the life that income supports. It pays for food and the roof overhead, household bills, transport, rent and the countless ordinary expenses that continue regardless of where an accident happened.
That's ultimately what the 6,330 claims represent: ordinary working lives interrupted by something that happened outside the workplace.
For a worker who's suddenly unable to earn, an accident at home can become a work problem very quickly; the place where the injury happens may be private, but the consequences rarely are.

Title: Ancom Nylex's Q1 profit jumps 15pct to RM24.13mil on higher RM533.42mil revenue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ancom Nylex Bhd's net profit rose 15.2 per cent to RM23.13 million in the first quarter ended Aug 31, 2026 lifted by its industrial chemicals segment.
Revenue for the quarter under review climbed to RM533.42 million from RM447.36 million a year ago.
Its industrial chemicals segment saw selling prices move higher alongside firmer crude oil prices.
The segment's revenue climbed 32.8 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to RM355.9 million from RM268 million previously, while pre-tax earnings almost doubled to RM19.4 million from RM10.2 million.
The improvement was largely attributable to healthier margins and higher operational efficiency in the segment's distribution business.
On the other hand, Agrichem generated revenue of RM136 million and pre-tax profit of RM24.2 million.
The company said the underlying rise in volume was masked by the stronger Ringgit against the US dollar which lowered the translated value of the segment's US dollar-denominated export sales.
Group chief executive officer and managing director Datuk Lee Cheun Wei said sales volumes in its agrichem segment continued to grow, reflecting sustained uptake across key export markets.
"Overall demand for our Agrichem products remains healthy. In Brazil specifically, the market's response to MSMA for soybean use has been promising since the product label was extended to cover the crop.
"Orders have been encouraging as
the planting season gets underway, and we expect this new market to contribute increasingly over time.
"We already have the production headroom to lift output further, which allows us to respond quickly as this market develops," he said in a statement.
However, he noted that the external environment continues to warrant a cautious approach.
Disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz have affected the flow of oil and natural gas, contributing to higher energy prices.
"While energy flows through the Strait have recovered in recent weeks, geopolitical and shipping risks remain elevated. These factors are weighing on business sentiment and the broader global economic outlook.
"We will continue to monitor these developments closely while pursuing the growth opportunities ahead," he added.

Title: 6,363 citizenship applications still under consideration, says Home Ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 6,363 citizenship applications remained under consideration as of Sept 30, following 16,338 applications received between Jan 1, 2024 and Sept 30 this year.
Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said 4,583 applications had been approved, with citizenship certificates issued.
"Each application will be thoroughly examined and considered based on the facts of the case, information, documents and supporting evidence submitted by the applicant, in turn, before a decision is made.
"The process requires detailed scrutiny, and no specific timeframe has been set for a decision to be made," he said.
He was responding to a question from Tan Kar Hing (PH-Gopeng) on the status of citizenship and entry permit applications during a Special Chamber sitting in the Dewan Rakyat.
On applications through naturalisation, he said the provision under Article 19(1) of the Federal Constitution applied to certain categories of adults born overseas to Malaysian mothers.
Shamsul Anuar said the provision could be considered for individuals aged 21 and above who had previously been unable to obtain Malaysian citizenship and faced difficulties meeting the residency requirements, subject to the prescribed criteria and conditions.
Among the requirements are residing in the Federation for at least 10 years within the 12 years preceding the application, including the 12 months immediately before the application; intending to reside permanently in Malaysia; being of good character; and having an adequate knowledge of the Malay language.
Applicants in this category must also obtain a Temporary Resident Identity Card (MyKAS) and hold it for at least six months before submitting their applications.

Title: Vestland bags RM225mil Kelantan river project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Vestland Bhd, through its indirect wholly-owned Vestland Infra Sdn Bhd, has secured a RM225.07 million contract for river widening and related works under the Integrated River Basin Development project in Kelantan.
Pembinaan Rizen Sdn Bhd awarded the contract, and Vestland Infra accepted the letter of award on Oct 15.
The scope covers river widening, structural and associated works.

Title: Astaka Padu and Kimlun in RM450mil Amora serviced residence project in Johor Bahru
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Astaka Padu Sdn Bhd and Kimlun Corporation Bhd have announced their latest joint development, the RM450 million gross development value Amora serviced residence.
This project represents the fourth collaboration between the two Johor-based groups and will be executed through their joint venture company, Astaka Kimlun Sdn Bhd.
Located on 2.45 acres of freehold commercial land in Tampoi, Johor Bahru, Amora serviced residence sits adjacent to the Pasir Gudang Highway and a 15-acre urban park.
The development is approximately a 15-minute drive from the Bukit Chagar Rapid Transit System station and the Johor Bahru Customs, Immigration and Quarantine Complex.
Amora serves as a key component of the Amora Park integrated development, which also includes 44 shop offices, a wellness mall and hotel, and an education hub. Earlier this month, all 44 shop offices were fully taken up within an hour of their launch.
The residence will consist of two towers—a 48-storey Tower A and a 45-storey Tower B—housing a total of 617 units.
Unit sizes will range from approximately 990 sq ft to 2,230 sq ft, with indicative selling prices starting from RM600,000.
Positioned as a "Modern Holiday Home with Park Living," the project targets larger households, holiday-home buyers, and multi-generational living, allocating between two and six car parks per unit.
The official launch is expected by the end of 2026.
"Despite concerns of normalization in the Johor Bahru residential market, we continue to see strong demand for projects with clear product differentiation, strong connectivity, good pricing and compelling lifestyle propositions," said Allen Khong, chief executive officer of Astaka Padu.
Meanwhile, Kimlun's executive director Chin Lian Hing said that the longstanding collaboration between the group and Astaka Padu demonstrated the complementary strengths of both groups.
"With Amora, we look forward to extending our successful partnership model and continuing to deliver quality developments that meet the evolving expectations of today's homebuyers," said Chin.

Title: 14, including two minors, charged with murder of 19-year-old youth in Gurun
Article:
GURUN: Fourteen people, including two teenagers, were charged at the magistrate's court here today with the murder of a 19-year-old youth last week.
The accused are Muhammad Asyraaf Muhammad Zaidi, 20; Muhammad Azrul Rahimi Muhamad Yusri, 18; Ahmad Izzul Irfan Ridduan, 21; Muhammad Rhahimy Abdul Rashid, 19; Yusman Hakimi Yusmezal, 24; Muhammad Zulfaqar Zulkarnain Khairol Fais, 21; and Muhammad Aiman Riduwan Abdullah, 21.
The other accused are Ahmad Aiman Danial Ahmad Wizam, 21; Muhammad Adam Haris Rosdan, 21; Muhammad Muqkriz Azizan, 21; Muhammad Adam Iqbal Mohd Wazir, 19; Syafiq Afif Syarafuddin Abd Ghapar, 23; and two minors aged 16 and 17.
They were jointly charged with murdering Muhammad Haikal Mohd Shahrilnizam, 19, at an unnumbered house in Jalan Sungai Petani here, between 9pm on Oct 5 and 7.30am on Oct 8.
However, no pleas were recorded after the charges were read out before magistrate Anis Suraya Ahmad, as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
They were charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same Act, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, and at least 12 strokes of the rotan upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Nik Nurhazirah Tuan Yahya led the prosecution.
Only three of the accused, Azrul Rahimi, Izzul Irfan and Zulfaqar Zulkarnain, were represented by lawyer Mohamad Ashraf Ahmad Sohaimi. The remaining accused were unrepresented.
The court fixed Dec 23 for the next mention of the case, pending the chemical and forensic reports.
Media reports previously stated that Haikal was allegedly held captive and tortured for two days before his body was dumped in the bushes near Jalan Harvard Golf Club on Oct 8.

Title: Next-of-kin of Long Lellang crash victims to receive RM130,000 in benefits, monthly pensions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The next-of-kin of four Health Ministry (MoH) staff who perished in a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak, will receive at least RM130,000 each in lump-sum benefits.
MoH said the payments, which were being coordinated with the Public Service Department (PSD) and Sarawak Health Department, comprised several benefits including payment for unutilised leave, derivative gratuity, funeral management assistance and the Death Ex-Gratia payment.
"The total lump-sum payment eligible to be received by each victim is not less than RM130,000," it said in a statement.
The ministry said eligible dependents would also begin receiving monthly derivative pensions from Oct 21, with payments distributed according to each beneficiary's entitlement under existing legal provisions.
"Pension sharing is implemented to ensure that each eligible dependent receives their respective entitlement based on existing legal provisions," it said.
It said PSD would provide further explanations to the eligible beneficiaries on the distribution of the pensions.
"In addition, the families would receive dependents' pensions and benefits under the Work Disaster Ex-Gratia Scheme, which are currently being processed by the Sarawak Pensions Division and the Finance Ministry," it said.
As a further tribute to the four personnel, the ministry said their posthumous promotions had been proposed and endorsed by the Public Service Promotion Board at its meeting on Oct 13.
It said it remained committed to expediting pension payments and other assistance to the victims' families through coordination with the relevant agencies.
"The ministry is aware that no amount of money can replace the loss of a loved one. The ministry hopes the assistance will, to some extent, ease the financial burden and daily affairs of the bereaved families," it said.
It was reported that a
Flying Doctor Service
Bo-105 helicopter carrying five people crashed near the Long Lellang STOLport in Sarawak on Tuesday, killing all on board.
CAAM said it received notification of the incident from the Flight Information Service at 3.58pm.

Title: UM student residence project to house 10,000 students by 2030
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Universiti Malaya's (UM) first phase of its student residence project is scheduled for completion in 2030, providing accommodation for 10,000 students amid concerns over university housing shortages.
UM vice-chancellor Professor Datuk Seri Dr Noor Azuan Abu Osman said the project, to be developed on a 4.17-hectare site at the university's Fifth Residential College, marked a significant step towards meeting students' accommodation needs.
"The project would provide more than physical accommodation, serving as a space for students to build friendships, develop leadership skills and pursue their ambitions," he said in his welcoming address at the launch of the UM Student Residence Project today.
Also present were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abdul Halim and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
Noor Azuan said he hoped the government would expedite the project, warning that students could graduate before its first block was built if implementation was delayed.
He said the initiative had taken nearly three years to progress through planning, consultations and government-level discussions.
"Universities are places where people think, but we must not overthink things to the point that students who enrol today graduate before the first block is built."
Universiti Malaya will work with a consortium of government-linked investment companies (GLICs) to develop the project. PBLT Sdn Bhd will deliver Phase 1, while Phase 2 will be developed with joint venture partners Malaysian Resources Corporation Berhad (MRCB) and Sime Darby Property Berhad.
The first phase, covering 4.17-hectare, is expected to accommodate 10,000 students upon completion in 2030. The second phase is planned to provide accommodation for up to 30,000 students.
Noor Azuan said UM had spent more than a year presenting the proposal to various agencies before Anwar announced, during the tabling of 2026 Budget on Oct 10 last year, that the university would pioneer the construction of student residences.
He said a special national strategic project monitoring meeting chaired by Anwar on Dec 15 last year established the project's development model, financing arrangements and implementation terms.
UM worked with the Higher Education Ministry, Finance Ministry, Economy Ministry, Public Private Partnership Unit (UKAS) and several companies to advance the project.
Noor Azuan said UM is not seeking shortcuts that would breach regulations, but wanted to avoid unnecessary delays now that the project's direction had been established.
He pledged that UM would monitor the project closely and ensure it was implemented transparently, in compliance with legal and governance requirements, while maintaining safety and reasonable accommodation rates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: E-Commerce Bill crucial for healthy digital economy, fair competition - MRCA
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The E-Commerce Bill is a crucial step toward fostering a healthy digital economy, protecting consumer interests, and upholding fair market competition, said the Malaysia Retail Chain Association (MRCA).
MRCA president Datuk Liew Bin emphasised that all businesses operating in Malaysia, domestic or foreign, must strictly adhere to statutory requirements regarding taxation, product safety, consumer protection, and commercial compliance. "We are not against foreign investment, nor are we opposed to e-commerce growth. Online and brick-and-mortar retail can complement each other to expand the market pie," he said in a statement today.
MRCA also recommended that the proposed legislation clearly delineate the liabilities of e-commerce platforms and merchants, tighten oversight on non-compliant goods, enhance seller verification and dispute resolution mechanisms, and enforce tax transparency to ensure cross-border sellers compete on an equal footing with local merchants.
Concurrently, MRCA said the government should scale up digital adoption support for domestic SMEs, helping them develop omnichannel capabilities, strengthen brand equity, and tap overseas markets. "We welcome competition, but it must be fair. A sustainable e-commerce ecosystem should not come at the expense of physical retail, but it must create mutual value for consumers, merchants, and the wider economy," it added.
Looking ahead, MRCA cautioned that the retail industry continues to grapple with rising overheads, including wages, rental, logistics, and inventory costs, alongside heightened competition from online players.
The association called on the government to broaden access to SME financing, digital adoption, artificial intelligence (AI) integration, talent upskilling, and homegrown brand development, while maintaining regular stakeholder engagements to assess policy outcomes.
Overall, MRCA acknowledged the positive signals delivered by Budget 2027 in key areas, but stressed that the true measure of the budget's success lies beyond allocations and policy announcements; it must translate into private investment, job creation, productivity gains, and robust consumption.
"We stand for fair remuneration for workers while ensuring businesses remain viable to create jobs; we embrace the digital economy while demanding a transparent and level playing field.
Only when the government, businesses, workers, and consumers benefit together can Malaysia's retail sector thrive sustainably and contribute more meaningfully to national economic growth," Liew Bin said.  —  BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rulers discuss bills on PM's tenure limit, separation of A-G and public prosecutor roles
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Conference of Rulers has discussed proposed constitutional amendments to limit the prime minister's tenure and separate the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor at its 273rd meeting.
The meeting, held at Istana Negara on Oct 14 and 15, also discussed the appointment of judges to the Special Court and proposed amendments to Section 97 of the Child Act.
According to a statement from the Keeper of the Rulers' Seal, the proposed constitutional amendment on limiting the prime minister's tenure was presented for consultation with the Conference of Rulers, while the amendment on separating the roles of the A-G and public prosecutor was presented for the conference's information.
The meeting was chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah.
All Rulers and state governors attended the first day of the meeting including the Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, Crown Prince of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra and Tunku Temenggong of Johor, Tunku Idris Iskandar Sultan Ibrahim.
On the second day of the meeting today, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia attended, accompanied by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The meeting also discussed the appointment of an occupant for the Malay Rulers' Institution Chair at Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM), as well as proposed dates for Conference of Rulers meetings in 2027.
Several matters concerning Islamic administration and affairs under the Malaysian National Council for Islamic Religious Affairs were also discussed, including a paper on expanding the scope of audits of zakat funds.
The Rulers were briefed on the latest developments in national security by Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, national defence by Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman, and the national economy by Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
