Title: PM Anwar vows to fast‑track UM hostel project, says no leakages or wastage allowed
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the Universiti Malaya (UM) Student Residence project to serve as a model for development management that is clean, efficient, and free from leakages or the wastage of public funds.
He said the implementation of this project must draw lessons from the shortcomings of past project management which led to cost overruns, delays, and abandoned construction sites ultimately resulting in losses for the nation.
“How much national funding has been wasted or lost due to poor management? Therefore, vice-chancellor, ensure that UM and this Student Residence project become an example for other agencies to emulate.
“You can do a great job, a clean job, an incorruptible job, and one carried out with full dedication. This is a real challenge for us,” he said during his inaugural address at the launch of the UM Student Residence project here today.
Also present were Minister of Higher Education Datuk Seri Dr. Zambry Abd Kadir and his deputy, Adam Adli Abd Halim; Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar; and UM vice-chancellor Prof Datuk Seri Dr Noor Azuan Abu Osman.
Anwar said the project in question is a major responsibility that must be carried out with full dedication, requiring the commitment of all involved parties to ensure it is completed according to plan.
He noted that the issue of “leakages” (inefficiencies or losses) does not stem from differences in race, region, or social class; rather, it is linked to dishonest conduct that undermines the national interest.
Consequently, the Prime Minister said he would personally oversee the project’s implementation. He also expressed his desire for it to be completed ahead of the original 2030 schedule, aiming to address the issue of student accommodation specifically the rising cost of house rentals in areas surrounding universities.
To ensure the project is expedited, Anwar said he has directed all government machinery including government-linked companies (GLCs) and government-linked investment companies (GLICs) to prioritise this initiative.
“This is a priority project for us that must be completed quickly. When you (Azuan) say it will be ready by 2030, I say no. This is a new, efficient Madani government. We will work to ensure it is accelerated,” he said.
The implementation of the UM Student Residence Development Project supports the government’s agenda as announced in the 2027 Budget to address student accommodation needs through infrastructure that is better planned, comfortable, and aligned with current requirements.
Designed to accommodate 40,000 students, the project will be executed in phases: Phase One will cater to 10,000 students, followed by Phase Two, which will provide additional capacity for another 30,000 students.
The residences will offer four categories of accommodation: ‘Standard’ (five rooms for 10 residents), ‘Standard Premium’ (three rooms for six residents), ‘Apartment’ (two rooms for three residents), and ‘Studio’ (for a single resident). All units are planned to be equipped with air-conditioning.
The project is based on a ‘community living’ concept, integrating residential functions with spaces for social interaction and community activities. This aims to foster an environment that encourages character development, social connections, and a sense of togetherness, thereby enriching the students’ overall experience throughout their studies.
Meanwhile, Deputy Minister of Higher Education Adam Adli Abd Halim, speaking to reporters after the event, expressed hope that this initiative would serve as a long-term, sustainable solution to issues concerning student accommodation.
He said the government is committed to ensuring the project proceeds smoothly through a ‘fast-track’ approach, without compromising on integrity or established management procedures.
“This project begins at UM, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), and Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin (UniSZA), with a second phase to follow. I believe we can expand this programme to other universities as well,” he said.
Earlier, in his speech, Azuan said the development of the Student Residences (*Residensi Siswa*) reflects the university’s commitment to prioritising student welfare, alongside its efforts to strengthen academic and research excellence.
“We cannot speak of excellence in higher education without addressing the realities of student life. The need for comfortable, safe, and affordable housing must be a core priority in the university’s development agenda.
“Through the Student Residences, UM aims to ensure that campus development is not focused solely on academic infrastructure, but also delivers tangible benefits to the daily lives of its students,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MOE reverts to haze plan: Schools shut at API 200, outdoor classes at 100, parents may keep kids home
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has reverted to the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK) guidelines, which mandate the immediate closure of schools when the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaches 200, following input from various relevant agencies.
Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said that under the PTJK, all outdoor classroom activities must also be halted when the API exceeds 100.
She added that parents are also permitted not to send their children to school if they are concerned that the haze condition could affect their health, provided they notify the school administration.
“In managing the haze, specific actions must be taken for each API reading level. We cannot assume that all risk levels require the same course of action,” she said in a Facebook post today.
She noted that the decision to return to the PTJK guidelines was made after discussions with related agencies, including taking into account views from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) that haze management must be guided by the said plan.
Fadhlina stated that the previous decision to take a more cautious approach was made by taking seriously the concerns expressed by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia regarding the haze situation, while prioritising the safety and health of students.
According to her, the MOE also received various feedback from parents, including requests for schools to be closed for a week, concerns about learning gaps, and the difficulty of managing childcare while working.
Therefore, she said the ministry called upon all relevant agencies such as the Ministry of Health, the Department of Environment (DOE), and the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) for discussions, as the issue involves health, air quality, and disaster management that require their expertise.
“I understand that logic. After all, an API reading of 150 is indeed within the unhealthy category. Parents’ concerns at that level are certainly well-founded,” she said.
Fadhlina stated that the flexibility given for students to be absent from school takes into account differing health conditions among students, including those suffering from asthma, respiratory issues, or those more easily affected by the haze.
She said the MOE is also responsible for ensuring that students do not continuously lose learning time, drawing from the experience during the Movement Control Order (MCO) which highlighted the difficulty of recovering missed learning, while emphasising that every concern will continue to be heard and decisions made in consultation with expert authorities. — Bernama

Title: Conference of Rulers deliberates PM term limits, AG‑PP separation and Child Act amendments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The proposed constitutional amendments to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure and separate the roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor were among the key matters discussed at the 273rd Conference of Rulers meeting at Istana Negara.
The two-day meeting, which began yesterday, was chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the second day’s proceedings, accompanied by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
According to a statement issued by the Office of the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal today, the Conference deliberated on a consultation paper concerning the Constitution (Amendment) Bill 2026, which proposes limiting the Prime Minister’s tenure.
The Conference was also briefed on the Constitution (Amendment) (No. 2) Bill 2026, concerning the separation of the roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor (AG-PP), as well as proposed amendments to Section 97 of the Child Act 2001.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail presented a briefing on national security, while Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman briefed the Conference on defence matters.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir also delivered an economic briefing.
Other matters discussed included the appointment of a Special Court judge, the appointment of the new chairholder for the Institution of Malay Rulers Chair at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), and proposed meeting dates for 2027.
The Conference also discussed matters concerning Islamic religious administration under the National Council for Islamic Religious Affairs Malaysia (MKI), including a proposal to expand the scope of audits of zakat funds.
The meeting was attended by the Malay Rulers and Governors, as well as the Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail, Crown Prince of Kelantan Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra, representing the Sultan of Kelantan, and the Tunku Temenggong of Johor Tunku Idris Iskandar Al-Haj, representing the Regent of Johor. — Bernama

Title: Selangor schools in Klang, Petaling, Gombak and more closed tomorrow as haze worsens
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 15 — Schools under the Klang, Kuala Selangor, Kuala Langat, Hulu Langat, Gombak, Sepang, Petaling Perdana and Petaling Utama district education offices will be closed tomorrow due to the haze.
However, the Selangor State Education Department (JPNS) said in a statement today that schools under the Hulu Selangor and Sabak Bernam district education offices will operate as usual.
“Nevertheless, all outdoor activities in both districts are prohibited.
“Parents, guardians, students and the wider education community are advised to take note of this announcement and refer to JPNS channels for the latest updates,” the statement said. — Bernama

Title: Sudden death probe opened after student’s fatal fall at Penang dormitory
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 15 — A female university student died after allegedly falling from a building in the hostel block of a higher education institute in Jalan Bukit Gambir, Gelugor here today.
Timur Laut district police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the police received a phone call from the university at 8.40am informing them of the discovery of the body of a 21-year-old female student residing in the dormitory.
The student’s body was found at 7.25am by the university’s cleaning staff. She was found lying on her back on the cement floor below the dormitory block. The student, suspected of having fallen from the building, was pronounced dead at the scene.
“Investigations at the scene found no signs of criminal elements, and further examination of the victim’s body revealed several external injuries suspected to have been caused by a fall from a height,” he said in a statement today.
The victim’s body has been sent to the Penang Hospital’s Forensic Department for an autopsy, and a sudden death report (LMM) has been opened to conduct an investigation into the case. — Bernama

Title: Penang statutory body chief pleads not guilty to 15 graft charges totalling RM800,000
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 15 — The chairman of a statutory body in Penang pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to 15 charges of accepting bribes totalling more than RM800,000 between June 2025 and July this year.
Datuk Dr Shaik Hussein Mydin, 53, is accused of corruptly receiving RM847,107.61 through Aliran Ilham Sdn Bhd (AISB) in multiple transactions from ATSH Management Sdn Bhd (ATSH) director Datuk R. Albert Suresh. The alleged bribes ranged from RM45.51 to RM244,620.
The payments were allegedly received as an inducement for appointing ATSH as a subcontractor to AISB for a RM23.27 million project to construct a 10-storey hostel block and facilities using the Industrialised Building System at Institut Kemahiran Tinggi PERDA in Bukit Panchor, Seberang Perai Selatan.
The alleged offences took place at a bank in Jalan Perda Selatan, Bandar Perda, in Seberang Perai Tengah, between June 26, 2025, and July 9, 2026.
The charges were brought under Section 16(a)(A) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009 (Act 694), which provides for a maximum prison term of 20 years and a fine of at least five times the value of the gratification involved, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) deputy public prosecutors Lim Jin Hong and Nurnajihatul Idayu Mohd Azuyar proposed bail of RM1 million, with additional conditions requiring the accused to surrender his passport, report to the MACC office monthly and refrain from interfering with prosecution witnesses.
Shaik Hussein was represented by a seven-member legal team led by Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, comprising Datuk Hasnal Rezua Merican, Mohd Shahrullah Khan, Simon Tan, Dr Shamsher Singh Thind, Muzzammil Merican and Intan Nur Alia Nodzri.
Amer Hamzah objected to the proposed bail amount, describing it as excessive and arguing that the prosecution had not provided sufficient factual grounds to justify the sum as necessary to ensure his client’s attendance in court.
Judge Irwan Suainbon granted the accused bail of RM300,000, subject to reporting to the MACC office once every two months and the other conditions proposed by the prosecution, and fixed Jan 8, 2027, for the submission of documents.
The court also allowed the accused to apply for the temporary release of his passport for specific periods and purposes, should the need arise. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal upholds 30‑year jail, 12 strokes for trader who hid step‑brother’s body in cement drum
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 15 — The Court of Appeal today upheld a 30-year jail sentence and 12 strokes of the cane imposed on a former trader for murdering his step-brother and concealing the body in a cement-filled drum.
A three-judge panel comprising Justices Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar unanimously dismissed Mohamad Zamhuri Azami’s appeal against his conviction and sentence.
The panel also dismissed the prosecution’s appeal to impose the death penalty on the 31-year-old accused.
Delivering the court’s unanimous decision, Justice Noorin said the sentence imposed by the High Court was appropriate and did not warrant appellate intervention.
“We also find no sufficient grounds to replace the sentence with the death penalty or a 40-year prison term, as requested by the prosecution,” she said.
Justice Noorin said the possibility of an argument or altercation between the appellant and the deceased did not, in itself, establish that the fatal act was justified under the defence of private defence.
She also said the prosecution had successfully established the necessary intention through the evidence presented, leaving no grounds to substitute the conviction with one under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
On May 13 last year, the Alor Setar High Court found Mohamad Zamhuri guilty of murdering Mohd Hasnul Nizar Khairul Anuar, 34, and sentenced him to 30 years in prison and 12 strokes of the cane.
The offence was committed at their home in Kampung Padang Hassan, Bukit Pinang, Alor Setar, Kedah, at 7.15pm on March 6, 2020.
According to the facts of the case, the appellant led police to the location where the victim’s body was concealed in a blue plastic drum filled with cement outside the house. Police also seized a meat-cleaving knife.
During today’s proceedings, defence counsel Ai Cha Ran argued that his client had not intended to kill his step-brother, claiming that the deceased had attacked him during an altercation and that he had acted in self-defence.
He further submitted that the evidence supported only a charge of culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code.
However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Aqilah Syaza Ariffin argued that the pathologist’s testimony showed that the victim’s injuries, particularly a long and deep incised wound to the neck, were inconsistent with the defence’s account of a fight or struggle. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s haze map turns red: Klang, Nilai, Shah Alam among worst affected at near‑200 API
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A total of 34 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5pm today, with Klang, Selangor recording the highest reading at 195.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Johor recorded eight areas with unhealthy readings — Pasir Gudang (184), Batu Pahat (179), Larkin and Tangkak (178 each), Pengerang (166), Kluang (165), Segamat (162) and Kota Tinggi (160).
In Selangor, apart from Klang, five other areas also recorded unhealthy API readings — Johan Setia (192), Shah Alam (180), Banting (174), Petaling Jaya (169) and Kuala Selangor (161), while in Negeri Sembilan, three areas recorded unhealthy readings - Nilai (191), Seremban (181) and Port Dickson (173).
Other areas with unhealthy API readings include Bukit Rambai (178), Melaka City (176) and Alor Gajah (175) in Melaka, Putrajaya (177), Cheras (174) and Batu Muda (166) in Kuala Lumpur, as well as Tanjung Malim (174), Seri Manjung (173), Pegoh, Ipoh (153) and Tasek, Ipoh (151) in Perak.
Meanwhile in Pahang, Temerloh (158), Jerantut (156), Rompin (154) and Indera Mahkota, Kuantan (135). recorded unhealthy API readings, along with Kemaman, Terengganu (138), Sandakan, Sabah (125) and Samarahan, Sarawak (117).
A total of 34 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while no areas recorded good air quality.
API readings between zero and 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 indicate moderate air quality, 101 to 200 indicate unhealthy air quality, 201 to 300 indicate very unhealthy air quality, while readings above 300 are classified as hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Dzulkefly: Families of MOH staff killed in Sarawak helicopter crash to receive pensions from Oct 21
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 15 — The next-of-kin of four Ministry of Health (MOH) staff who perished in a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak, will begin receiving monthly derivative pension payments starting Oct 21.
This initiative is part of the government’s commitment to ensuring the continued well-being of the victims’ families.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said MOH, in collaboration with the Public Service Department (PSD) and the Sarawak State Health Department, has managed the disbursement of derivative pension benefits and appropriate financial assistance to the next-of-kin in a comprehensive and prudent manner.
He noted that the total lump-sum payments for which the next-of-kin are eligible include compensation for accumulated leave (GCR), a derivative gratuity, funeral expense assistance, and an ex-gratia death payment.
“Alhamdulillah… the well-being of the families of the four MOH staff members who perished in the Long Lellang crash remains a priority for the Madani Government and MOH,” he said in a post on X today.
Dzulkefly added that a proposal for the posthumous promotion of the four healthcare workers has also been approved as a mark of the highest respect for their service and sacrifices.
“May this support help ease the daily burdens of the bereaved families. My deepest condolences go out to all the families of the victims. Our prayers remain with them...” he said.
Earlier, MOH said the total lump-sum payment for each victim amounts to no less than RM130,000, comprising compensation for accumulated leave (GCR), a derivative gratuity, funeral expense assistance, and an ex-gratia death payment.
The Ministry of Health further explained that the derivative pension will be distributed among eligible beneficiaries according to their respective shares, with the allocation structured to ensure that every entitled dependent receives their due portion in accordance with existing legal provisions.
The Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang on September 8 claimed the lives of five individuals, including four healthcare personnel who were on official duty providing services to a remote community. — Bernama

Title: KL police chief: Chemistry, pathology reports pending in custodial death case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Police are awaiting the full report from the Chemistry Department and official pathology results to complete their investigation into the recent death of a man in police custody.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the cause of death of the local man, who was in his 40s, had yet to be determined pending the reports.
He said the investigation was being conducted independently and thoroughly by the Bukit Aman Death in Custody Criminal Investigation Unit (USJKT), in collaboration with the Integrity and Standards Compliance Department (JIPS).
“The investigation is being conducted from various angles, taking into account all necessary evidence. We ask all parties to be patient and allow the police time to complete the investigation,” he told a press conference here today.
Fadil also urged the public to refrain from commenting or speculating on the case, warning that the dissemination of unverified information could be misleading and cause public concern.
Outlining the chronology of events, he said the man had been detained to assist in investigations into three separate police reports involving drug-related offences and other crimes.
“A record check revealed that the deceased had 44 criminal records, comprising 18 drug-related cases and 26 other criminal offences. He had also admitted to involvement in 17 other housebreaking and theft cases in the Cheras district,” he said.
Fadil said the man was detained in accordance with established standard operating procedures (SOPs). However, he reportedly fell ill while in custody and was taken to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) for further treatment.
“The suspect was confirmed to have died at 1.52 am on Oct 1 while receiving treatment at the hospital,” he said.
Previously, Lawyers for Liberty (LFL) urged police to investigate the death as a homicide following allegations that the man had sustained serious injuries to his body. — Bernama

Title: Woman brushing teeth behind wheel flashes middle finger before kicking auxiliary cop in groin at Glo Damansara
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A woman who was allegedly brushing her teeth behind the wheel flashed her middle finger at an auxiliary police officer before getting out of her car and kicking him in the groin during a bizarre confrontation at Glo Damansara yesterday.
The woman then managed to escape after a struggle with the 30-year-old officer, leaving police hunting for her following the incident in Taman Tun Dr Ismail (TTDI).
According to
Utusan Malaysia
, the drama unfolded at about 8.38am when the officer, who was on stationary duty, spotted a Hyundai Inokom parked facing the wrong direction.
The driver was also allegedly honking at other vehicles for no apparent reason.
Brickfields district police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the officer approached the car to reprimand the woman and instruct her to move her vehicle.
But instead of complying, the woman allegedly responded with an obscene gesture — all while brushing her teeth.
“However, the suspect made an obscene gesture by raising her middle finger while brushing her teeth.
“The suspect then got out of the vehicle and attempted to attack the officer before kicking him in the groin,” Hoo said, as quoted by the national daily.
The officer called for backup as he struggled with the woman and attempted to detain her, but she managed to flee before other personnel could intervene.
Police have since launched a search for the suspect.
“Efforts are actively underway to locate the suspect.
“The case is being investigated under Section 323 of the Penal Code and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955,” Hoo said.
Section 323 covers voluntarily causing hurt, while Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act concerns insulting behaviour.

Title: Selangor, Putrajaya, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang schools stay open tomorrow amid haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — All educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Negeri Sembilan, Pahang, Selangor, and Putrajaya will operate as usual tomorrow.
In separate statements today, the State Education Departments (JPN) in the three states and the Putrajaya Federal Territory Education Department (JPWPP) encouraged all pupils, teachers, support staff (AKP), and school personnel to wear face masks.
The statements noted that parents and guardians concerned about the health effects of the haze on their children are permitted to keep them at home, provided they notify the school of the absence.
In Negeri Sembilan, the JPN said all outdoor activities — including physical education, co-curricular and sports activities, camps, celebrations, assemblies, and open-hall events — must cease if the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeds 100.
The department added that any decision to close educational institutions due to the haze remains subject to ministry criteria and guidelines based on API readings and prevailing conditions.
Meanwhile, in Pahang, Selangor, qnd Putrajaya, the respective state education departments and the JPWPP said all outdoor activities have been suspended due to the haze.
In Penang, the Penang State Education Department (JPNPP) announced that all educational institutions under its purview will also operate as usual tomorrow, but all outdoor classroom activities must be postponed.
“As of 2pm, Oct 15, API readings at all monitoring stations in the state were recorded below the 150 level. Pupils attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a health protection measure,” it said in a statement.
The statement also noted that parents or guardians concerned about their children’s health following the haze situation may consider keeping them home, provided they notify the school authorities.
Parents and guardians are also advised to obtain updates through official communication channels, such as the JPN, JPWPP, District Education Offices (PPD), and schools.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, 34 areas recorded unhealthy API readings as at 9am today, with Johan Setia in Selangor registering the highest at 192. — Bernama

Title: Honeymoon hiccup: Malaysian couple’s car triggers Bangkok bomb scare
Article:
BANGKOK, Oct 15 — A Malaysian couple on their honeymoon in Thailand sparked a security alert in Bangkok on Wednesday after their car was found parked in a prohibited area, prompting authorities to call in an Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) team to inspect the vehicle.
Metropolitan Police Bureau Commissioner Pol Lt Gen Siam Boonsom said the Malaysian-registered red car was found parked on the pavement along Sukhumvit 17 Lane in Bangkok’s Lumpini district, raising concerns amid heightened security for the ongoing IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings 2026.
He said Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) officials spotted the vehicle during a patrol on Wednesday afternoon and alerted the authorities over concerns that it might contain hazardous materials.
“EOD officers were called in to inspect the vehicle. They found seven fuel containers holding a total of 40 litres of petrol, but no illegal items,” he told reporters on Thursday.
Siam, who did not disclose details of the Malaysian couple, said they were questioned, and police established that they had arrived in Thailand on Oct 11 for their honeymoon.
They were travelling to several provinces in their private car and were scheduled to return to Malaysia on Oct 17.
He said the couple explained that they had purchased the extra fuel at a petrol station in Malaysia because they were unfamiliar with the routes and wanted to carry reserve fuel for emergencies.
According to Siam, the couple said they had parked at the location to visit a shopping mall after a local taxi driver advised them that parking was permitted there.
“Preliminary checks found no illegal items in the vehicle, and the amount of fuel did not exceed the legal limit. However, they were fined 2,000 baht (about RM243.25) for parking in a clearly marked no-parking zone,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Selangor launches SA500 financing scheme for SMEs, NINE super app to consolidate services
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Selangor today launched a financing initiative for businesses facing cash flow constraints alongside a super app intended to bring government services, payments and mobility options onto a single digital platform.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said Selangor Advance 500 (SA500) would help eligible companies and contractors undertaking state-related projects manage their cash flow, while the NINE Super App would make government services and everyday transactions more accessible to the public.
Amirudin said the initiatives reflected the state government's commitment to supporting business growth and ensuring more people could benefit from the digital economy.
“In line with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s emphasis on the vital role of SMEs in Malaysia’s economy, the Selangor state government is committed to strengthening support for these businesses, enabling them to grow further and compete with companies across Southeast Asia,” he said on Facebook.
Amirudin said access to financing remained a challenge for many businesses, with SA500 intended to ease cash flow pressures and help eligible companies sustain their operations.
According to Selangor Advance's official website, the financing programme provides Shariah-compliant facilities to small and medium enterprises (SMEs), including contractors and suppliers serving government agencies, government-linked companies and eligible private companies.
The facilities include invoice financing, working capital financing, performance bonds and other financial support for different stages of a business or project.
According to Selangor Advance's published terms, the programme offers financing facilities to eligible businesses to help them manage cash flow, including by obtaining early payment for outstanding invoices, subject to its terms and conditions.
Amirudin said the second initiative, NINE, was intended to simplify access to public services by consolidating them within one application.
“The NINE Super App brings government services, assistance, payments and mobility into one platform, making everyday transactions simpler for the rakyat,” he said.
The app already offers an electronic wallet, digital parking payments and access to other services, including bill payments and transport-related transactions. Further integration of Selangor government services is planned as the platform develops.
The initiative is also intended to reduce the need for residents to use multiple applications to deal with different state agencies and local authorities.
Amirudin said the two initiatives would complement each other by strengthening the business community while improving access to public services.
“Together, SA500 and NINE advance the State Government’s vision of a more inclusive digital society and a stronger business community.
“By improving access to financing and public services, we are creating more opportunities for Selangor’s businesses and people to thrive,” he said.

Title: Seven seats in play, 21 firmly held: Zahid stakes out BN’s position in Melaka
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has said it will retain the 21 seats it won in the previous Melaka state election, leaving Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) component parties to negotiate over the remaining seven constituencies as discussions over electoral cooperation continue ahead of next month’s polls.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition was holding talks with PN’s core parties following the suspension of activities by the Opposition coalition, but made clear that BN had no intention of giving up the seats it currently holds.
“Our principle is that the 21 seats we won are not seats that we intend to share,” he told reporters in Beijing today, according to
The Star
.
“If there is to be any sharing, it may involve seat swaps, but those 21 seats will remain ours.
“Any negotiations will concern the seven remaining seats that are not held by Barisan.
“It will be up to the other parties to decide how they distribute those seats among themselves.”
The deputy prime minister is in China on a five-day working visit aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, technology and vocational education. Earlier today, he held talks with Chinese Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang in Beijing.
Zahid also suggested that the prospect of cooperation with Pakatan Harapan (PH), BN’s partner in the federal unity government, had diminished.
He said statements by PH leaders at both national and state levels indicated that the coalition had lost interest in working with BN for the Melaka election.
“We respect that position,” he said.
Zahid added that Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh had been entrusted with making the final decision on BN’s electoral cooperation in the state.
The coalition is expected to announce its decision before nomination day on October 31.
The latest remarks follow comments by Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki on October 13 that BN was in the final stages of seat negotiations, with the coalition determined to defend all 21 constituencies it secured in the previous state election.
BN secured a commanding majority in the November 2021 Melaka election, winning 21 of the 28 state assembly seats, while PH took five and PN two.
The Election Commission has fixed November 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka state election, with nominations scheduled for October 31.

Title: Pushing mega-projects, Hamzah Zainudin criticises Budget 2027 as ‘lacking vision’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today criticised Budget 2027 as “lacking vision”, arguing that the federal government’s spending plan lacks a long-term economic plan and relies heavily on short-term handouts.
Hamzah (PN-Larut) cited the government’s failure to meet its target of RM90 billion in development expenditure for two consecutive years, arguing this indicates poor fiscal management that could fuel concerns about potential under-investment in infrastructure projects.
The Larut MP suggested large-scale infrastructure projects to serve as primary “engines of growth”.
“I mean he (Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim) has tabled five budgets already but still has not shown any clear ideas for the future. This clearly shows this government lacks vision,” he said at a press conference here.
“Even if you look at development expenditure, it was he that set the RM90 billion target. That is in the 13th Malaysian Plan, yet the devex (he’s announced) for two straight years didn’t meet the target… isn’t this the very waad (vow) you made?”
Anwar tabled a record RM459 billion federal spending plan for next year, of which some RM83 billion is earmarked for development. The rest will go to operating expenses, the bulk being pension payments and emoluments.
Hamzah suggested there should have been more for development spending. He proposed mega infrastructure projects such as a major highway connecting Malaysia’s east and west coasts, or new sea ports to improve logistics efficiency, enhance supply chains, and boost regional trade connectivity.
Still, Hamzah and the Opposition have also been accused of lacking ideas. Government leaders often point out that Perikatan Nasional has failed to produce a single shadow budget since 2022, which they said reflected the coalition’s lack of vision or ideological coherence.
When asked why PN has not produced its own budgets, Hamzah called it a futile exercise.
“As the Opposition we are asked about producing alternative budgets. My question is: can they be implemented? If can’t then what is the point? It becomes a self-indulgent exercise,” he said.
“What we do is we debate to correct policies (under the Budget) that we feel are weak and not beneficial to the people, and we feel the views we express should be considered by the government.”

Title: Veterinary extension officers key to Malaysia’s food security, says deputy minister
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 15 — Veterinary extension officers play a crucial role in bridging government policies, the expertise of the Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and the farming community to boost livestock productivity and strengthen national food security.
Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said the effectiveness of veterinary extension services should be measured by improvements at farm level, including lower mortality rates among young livestock, increased milk yields and animal weights, and higher incomes for farmers.
“Policies and targets will only yield results when they reach livestock farmers in the form of the right knowledge and practices.
“Therefore, Scheduled Planned Visits and Gross Margin Analysis must be implemented systematically to evaluate the effectiveness of interventions using concrete data and evidence,” he said when officiating the 2026 Veterinary Extension Convention here today.
Themed “Veterinary Extension: A Driver for Productivity and Food Security”, the convention was also attended by Veterinary Services Department director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Noor Hisham Mohd Haron.
Chan said Malaysia’s import dependency rate for beef and buffalo meat stood at 82.6 per cent in 2025, while the rate for goat and sheep meat was 90.7 per cent.
To address this dependency, he said the ministry was targeting domestic production of about 50,000 metric tonnes of beef and buffalo meat this year, with the self-sufficiency ratio (SSR) projected to increase to 18 per cent.
He said the target was supported by 68 satellite farms across seven states, which had produced more than 45,000 head of livestock.
“This strategic direction is reinforced by the National Food Security Policy 2030 (DKMN 2030), which outlines efforts to strengthen the livestock breeding industry, maximise domestic ruminant and dairy production, and bolster extension services as a catalyst for human capital development,” he said.
Chan also outlined three key priorities for the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security: data-driven advisory services, better coordination of assistance among agencies, and building farmers’ trust through consistent guidance and follow-ups.
At the event, he launched three DVS guidebooks on good animal husbandry practices covering dairy cattle, goats and sheep, and feedlot cattle.
“Congratulations to the DVS on these publications. I hope the guidelines will be fully utilised for training and field guidance rather than merely serving as shelf decoration,” he said.
Chan also presented Perak DVS with the Overall Champion award for Best Extension Services, which came with RM500 in cash and a certificate of appreciation.
This year, 78 nominations were received across eight competition categories covering various aspects of veterinary extension services and projects.
The categories included Best State Veterinary Service, Best District Veterinary Service, Best Livestock-Based Industry Development Project, Best Veterinary Extension Project, Best Veterinary Extension Project Poster, Best Veterinary Extension Project Video Presentation, Best Veterinary Extension Mentor/Officer and Best VetEC (Veterinary Extension Centre) Operation. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: RM130M boost for local film, music, and creative content
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The allocation of more than RM130 million under Budget 2027 for the local film, music and creative industries is a timely move to boost the sector’s contribution to economic growth and talent development.
MyCreative Ventures said in a statement today that the government’s support would help industry players nurture their talents, create high-quality content and build more resilient and sustainable creative businesses.
“In an industry increasingly shaped by technology, digital content and global competition, creativity must extend beyond producing works to generating greater economic value,” it said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027 on Oct 9, announced an allocation of more than RM130 million to support the local film, music and creative content industries, with the aim of elevating Malaysia’s image, creating job opportunities and bringing Malaysian stories to a global audience.
On the full exemption of entertainment duty on tickets for local film screenings and theatrical performances in the Federal Territories, MyCreative Ventures said the measure would help stimulate demand for local works, widen public access to quality content and boost the earnings of industry players.
“More importantly, the initiative will help build a stronger domestic market, paving the way for Malaysian creative works and talent to expand their reach.
“MyCreative Ventures will continue to support the development of the nation’s creative economy through value creation, stronger industry capabilities, the development and commercialisation of intellectual property, and broader access to markets and business opportunities,” the statement read.
Meanwhile, MyCreative Ventures Group chairman Datuk Muhammad Bakhtiar Wan Chik said the allocation underscored the MADANI Government’s continued commitment to developing the creative industry into a competitive, high-value sector that contributes more significantly to the national economy. — Bernama

Title: Kepong knife attack: Chinese student charged with stabbing ex-girlfriend and her brother
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A 20-year-old Chinese national university student pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to two charges of causing grievous hurt by stabbing his former girlfriend and her younger brother with a knife last month.
Chen Jun is accused of causing grievous hurt to Leong Kai Ting, 21, and her younger brother, Leong Shun Jie, 18, by stabbing them both with a knife capable of causing death. The alleged offences took place at a house in Taman Sri Bintang, Kepong, at 5 am on Sept 29.
The charges were brought under Section 326 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum prison term of 20 years and is liable to a fine or caning upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Nurainizatul Farhana Zainal did not offer bail, saying the offences were non-bailable.
“Should the court decide to grant bail, the prosecution requests that it be set at RM8,000 with two local sureties, and that the accused surrender his passport to the court,” she said.
Chen Jun’s lawyer Ling Yee Siew urged the court to reduce the bail amount, submitting that her client was pursuing a finance degree at a private university and did not pose a flight risk.
“According to a medical report dated Sept 14 from a private hospital, my client is suffering from depression.
“I therefore seek lower bail to enable him to obtain follow-up treatment for a leg injury he sustained through self-harm while experiencing depression,” she said. Chen Jun appeared in court in a wheelchair.
Judge Suhaila Haron granted Chen Jun bail of RM8,000 with two Malaysian sureties, subject to the prosecution’s additional conditions.
She then fixed Nov 11 for case mention. — Bernama

Title: Perikatan ‘almost 100pc’ certain of Melaka election alliance, but Takiyuddin keeps potential partners under wraps
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is almost certain to forge an alliance with other political parties ahead of the Melaka state election, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today, although he stopped short of revealing who its potential partners might be.
According to
Utusan Malaysia
, Takiyuddin put the likelihood of cooperation at nearly 100 per cent when questioned about the Opposition coalition’s preparations for the upcoming polls.
“It’s around 100 per cent. Not more than 100 per cent,” he told a press conference in Parliament.
His remarks come just two days after Barisan Nasional (BN) suggested it was close to securing an electoral partner, with negotiations said to have reached 90 per cent mutual understanding.
However, BN has insisted that any potential ally must be trustworthy and would not “stab it in the back”.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki declined to identify the parties involved in the discussions but hinted at the kind of political partners BN would be willing to work with.
Takiyuddin did not disclose which parties PN was negotiating with or whether the talks involved BN.
He said discussions over seat allocations were already under way, both with potential allies and among PN’s own component parties.
“Discussions have been ongoing for some time between us and the parties cooperating with us, as well as among our own component parties.
“We are discussing seat allocations and the necessary thorough preparations that we need to make,” he said.
The uncertainty over PN’s electoral arrangements comes as the coalition faces a separate legal obstacle that could prevent it from contesting under its own name and logo.
The Registrar of Societies (RoS) suspended all PN activities with effect from September 23, leaving the coalition unable to use its name and symbol while the order remains in force.
Asked how PN intended to contest the election if the suspension was not lifted, Takiyuddin said alternative arrangements were already being considered but declined to elaborate.
“There is an alternative for everything. The first option, of course, is the Perikatan Nasional logo. If that cannot be used, there are other alternatives, but these are strategies that cannot be disclosed.
“Otherwise, it wouldn’t be a strategy. If we announce it, it becomes a tragedy,” he quipped.
The Melaka state election is scheduled for November 14, with nominations on October 31 and early voting on November 10, following the dissolution of the state assembly on September 23.
In the previous election in 2021, BN secured a commanding majority with 21 of the 28 seats, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won five and PN two.
The coalition’s legal difficulties follow notices issued by the RoS on September 22 concerning its registration and activities.
On Tuesday, the Kuala Lumpur High Court granted PN permission to challenge the RoS action through a judicial review but refused its application for an immediate stay of the suspension order.
Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad ruled that PN could proceed with its legal challenge but declined to temporarily lift the suspension pending further proceedings.
The court has fixed October 22 to hear PN’s application for a stay of the order, with both sides given an opportunity to present their arguments.
Until then, PN remains barred from using its name and logo, while its activities remain suspended, complicating its preparations for the Melaka election.

Title: Court hears charges against former UKM director accused of RM3.12m contract abuse
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 15 — A former director of an education centre at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to two charges of abusing his position to secure employment contracts worth RM3.12 million in 2022.
Datuk Prof Muhammad Hussin, 64, a retiree, entered the plea after the charges were read out before Judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin.
According to the charges, Muhammad, a member of Koperasi Siswazah Bangi Berhad (KSBB), allegedly abused his position to secure two contracts worth RM1.2 million and RM1.92 million respectively to manage the Master of Education programme through UKM’s Faculty of Education.
He was accused of influencing KSBB board members at two separate meetings to approve the appointment of QTech Management Malaysia Sdn Bhd, a company in which he purportedly had an interest, as the programme operator.
The alleged offences took place on Feb 26 and June 25, 2022, at Kolej Keris Mas, UKM, and Hotel Tenera in Bangi, respectively.
Muhammad was charged under Section 23(1) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009 (Act 694), which carries a maximum prison term of 20 years and a fine of at least five times the value of the gratification involved, if it can be valued or is monetary in nature, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
MACC deputy public prosecutor Muaz Ahmad Khairuddin proposed bail of RM300,000, with additional conditions requiring the accused to report to the MACC office, surrender his passport to the court and refrain from interfering with prosecution witnesses.
Defence counsel Muhammad Wafi Anwar Roslan sought a lower bail of RM50,000, citing his client’s financial circumstances, including his responsibility for two wives and nine children, and his reliance on a monthly pension as his sole source of income.
“The accused also suffers from synovial sarcoma and heart disease, both of which require regular treatment. I also urge the court not to impose the passport surrender condition, as his second wife and child are in Indonesia,” he said.
The court set bail at RM80,000 and ordered the accused to surrender his passport and refrain from interfering with prosecution witnesses.
The case was fixed for mention on Nov 12. — Bernama

Title: Zetrix AI pledges cooperation as police, MACC probe unpaid RM314m collections
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Zetrix AI Bhd will fully cooperate with authorities in an ongoing joint investigation by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the company said its operations remained unaffected by the investigation.
The company was responding to a query from Bursa Malaysia Securities dated Oct 14 regarding a media report entitled "Police say six witnesses questioned in probe into MyEG, Zetrix AI” published by The Edge Malaysia on Oct 13.
Zetrix AI said it would communicate any material developments through official announcements.
The company said it would make necessary announcements on material developments as appropriate. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak man finds RM1b in bank account, asks ChatGPT to count the zeros — only to discover it’s a glitch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — When a Sarawak clinic manager opened his banking app and discovered a mysterious 10-digit balance, he did what some people might do when faced with an eye-watering number: he asked ChatGPT.
The answer? A whopping RM1 billion.
But for Wan Muhammad Fairus, 33, whose account should have contained less than RM1,000, his unexpected brush with billionaire status was over almost as quickly as it began.
According to
Berita Harian
, the father of four from Samariang, Kuching, was in his bedroom preparing to make a banking transaction when he stumbled upon the extraordinary balance.
“I was in my bedroom at the time, about to make a transaction. If I’m not mistaken, I had less than RM1,000 in my account. When I opened the app and tapped the icon to reveal my balance, I was shocked to see such an enormous amount of money.
“I was completely stunned! My hands were shaking as I held my phone. I tried logging out and logging back in, but the money was still there.
“It was only after checking my bank statement and asking ChatGPT how much the figure amounted to that I realised it was RM1 billion,” he said with a laugh when contacted by the newspaper.
The bizarre discovery soon caught the attention of social media users after Wan Muhammad Fairus shared a screenshot of his online banking app showing the astonishing 10-digit figure.
But rather than start planning how to spend his newfound fortune, he suspected something was amiss.
Knowing the money was not his, he contacted the bank to find out what had gone wrong.
He said he never considered touching the windfall, aware that spending money mistakenly credited to his account could land him in legal trouble.
“After I contacted the bank, they informed me that there had been a technical problem and temporarily froze my account until 4pm yesterday.
“Everything was resolved after the bank reversed the transaction, and the money originally in my account was unaffected,” he said.
And while his billionaire moment may have been short-lived, there could still be a little something in it for him.
Wan Muhammad Fairus said the bank had mentioned the possibility of a reward, although he had yet to receive anything or find out what it might be.
“The bank also mentioned that they wanted to give me a reward, but I haven’t received anything yet and don’t know what it will be. Perhaps I’ll have to wait for an email notification or an announcement from them,” he said.
For now, his account is back to normal — and his extraordinary billion-ringgit surprise has become a story to tell.

Title: Health Ministry races to stock aerochambers and nebulisers as haze drives surge in respiratory cases
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Health Ministry (MOH) has increased stocks of medical equipment at healthcare facilities nationwide to prepare for a potential rise in haze-related illnesses, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the additional supplies comprised 841 adult aerochambers, 396 paediatric aerochambers and 576 nebulisers to cater for a possible surge in respiratory cases.
He said the ministry had also activated the National Haze Operations Room on Sept 4 and was closely monitoring three main health conditions, namely upper respiratory tract infections (URTI), asthma and conjunctivitis, through 78 sentinel healthcare facilities.
“Through the Crisis Preparedness and Response Centre (CPRC), the ministry is stepping up public health measures in response to rising Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and deteriorating air quality caused by open burning,” he said when replying to a question from Cha Kee Chin (PH-Rasah).
Cha had wanted to know the ministry’s initiatives to mitigate the impact of haze on public health and inter-agency cooperation in monitoring air quality and protecting vulnerable groups.
Dzulkefly said monitoring at 78 sentinel healthcare facilities nationwide showed that URTI cases surged by 167.21 per cent to 7,065 in epidemiological week 36, compared with 2,644 cases the previous week, due to deteriorating air quality.
On cooperation with other agencies, he said the Health Ministry had been providing technical advice to the Education Ministry and the Higher Education Ministry on suspending outdoor activities when the API exceeds 100, as well as recommending school closures when the reading exceeds 200.
He said the ministry also worked closely with the Department of Environment, the Malaysian Meteorological Department and the National Disaster Management Agency to ensure early warnings and preventive measures were communicated effectively to the public. — Bernama

Title: Teenagers among 14 charged in Gurun murder, victim allegedly tortured before body found near golf club
Article:
GURUN, Oct 15 — Fourteen individuals, including two teenagers, were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with the murder of a 19-year-old youth last week.
The accused are Muhammad Asyraaf Muhammad Zaidi, 20; Muhammad Azrul Rahimi Muhamad Yusri, 18; Ahmad Izzul Irfan Ridduan, 21; Muhammad Rhahimy Abdul Rashid, 19; Yusman Hakimi Yusmezal, 24; Muhammad Zulfaqar Zulkarnain Khairol Fais, 21; and Muhammad Aiman Riduwan Abdullah, 21.
The other accused are Ahmad Aiman Danial Ahmad Wizam, 21; Muhammad Adam Haris Rosdan, 21; Muhammad Muqkriz Azizan, 21; Muhammad Adam Iqbal Mohd Wazir, 19; Syafiq Afif Syarafuddin Abd Ghapar, 23; and two teenagers aged 16 and 17.
They were jointly charged with murdering Muhammad Haikal Mohd Shahrilnizam, 19, at an unnumbered house in Jalan Sungai Petani here, between 9pm on Oct 5 and 7.30am on Oct 8.
However, no pleas were recorded after the charges were read out before Magistrate Anis Suraya Ahmad, as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
They were charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same Act, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, and at least 12 strokes of the cane upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Nik Nurhazirah Tuan Yahya led the prosecution. Only three of the accused, Muhammad Azrul Rahimi, Ahmad Izzul Irfan and Muhammad Zulfaqar Zulkarnain, were represented by lawyer Mohamad Ashraf Ahmad Sohaimi. The remaining accused were unrepresented.
The court fixed Dec 23 for the next mention of the case, pending the chemical and forensic reports.
Media reports previously stated that Muhammad Haikal was allegedly held captive and tortured for two days before his body was dumped in the bushes near Jalan Harvard Golf Club on Oct 8. — Bernama

Title: Lim Guan Eng urges Malaysia to sue Indonesia over haze if Jakarta rejects Asean firefighting task force
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has urged Malaysia to consider legal action against Indonesia to seek compensation for the worsening transboundary haze crisis if Jakarta refuses to cooperate with a proposed permanent Asean firefighting task force.
Lim said the recurring crisis, which has forced schools to close and disrupted livelihoods, could no longer be treated as an annual inconvenience, calling for a coordinated regional response to tackle forest and land fires at their source.
In his speech during the Budget 2027 debate in the Dewan Rakyat today, the former finance minister proposed establishing a permanent Asean task force involving Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and the Philippines, with rescue personnel available throughout the year to respond swiftly to outbreaks of forest and land fires.
The call comes as Malaysia continues to grapple with deteriorating air quality caused by smoke from forest and land fires in Indonesia, with 34 of the country’s 68 air monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am today.
Klang and Johan Setia in Selangor recorded the highest readings at 192, approaching the very unhealthy threshold of 201. The haze has also disrupted daily life, with schools in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and several states ordered to close on October 9 to protect students from exposure to polluted air.
“If the Indonesian government continues to reject the Asean task force on grounds of national sovereignty, the Malaysian government will have no choice but to initiate legal action to seek compensation,” he said, according to the text of his speech.
“Malaysians can no longer remain silent and take no action in the face of this recurring haze crisis.”
The DAP national adviser said forest and land fires in Indonesia had affected an estimated 300,000 hectares this year, an area more than 70 per cent larger than that recorded in 2025.
He also criticised Jakarta for what he described as its reluctance to accept foreign assistance, including offers from Malaysia, despite the growing scale of the fires.
“It is deeply regrettable that the Indonesian government has refused to continue accepting international assistance from Japan, which has already ended, or to promptly accept offers of assistance from foreign countries, including Malaysia,” he said.
“Its justification is that Indonesia is capable of handling the forest and land fires, although the reality suggests otherwise.”
Lim argued that a permanent regional response team, rather than temporary arrangements activated only during emergencies, would allow ASEAN countries to tackle fires before the resulting smoke spread across national borders.
He also called on the Malaysian government to provide financial assistance to people whose incomes have been affected by the haze, particularly gig economy workers and Grab drivers who rely on outdoor work.
“Our schools have been closed, while workers, particularly those in the gig economy and Grab drivers, have been forced to stop working because of the haze crisis,” he said.
“The long-term health effects have yet to be determined. In short, the government should provide financial assistance to those affected.”
Lim said the haze was threatening not only public health and children’s safety but also Malaysia’s economic prosperity, making a lasting regional solution increasingly urgent.
His proposals formed part of a wider speech in support of Budget 2027, which was tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on October 9.
The haze has become a growing regional concern, with fires in Indonesia affecting air quality across neighbouring countries, including Malaysia and Singapore.
On October 11, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Malaysia was still awaiting Indonesia’s response to its offer to send a firefighting aircraft, three helicopters and 52 personnel to help tackle the blazes, according to Bernama.
Indonesia, meanwhile, said on October 13 that it would assess foreign offers of assistance based on their effectiveness in supporting firefighting operations, according to CNA.

Title: Prisons Department probes Kajang jail after NGO flags water shortages, dirty food trays and poor hygiene
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Prisons Department is investigating allegations by a non-governmental organisation (NGO) concerning water supply disruptions, sanitation facilities and food provision at Kajang Prison.
In a statement today, the department said the investigation was aimed at establishing the actual situation and ensuring that the issues raised received appropriate attention.
At the same time, priority will be given to immediate improvements to address any shortcomings identified, particularly those involving basic facilities, hygiene and inmates’ welfare,” the statement said.
The department said it consistently prioritised inmates’ welfare, health, hygiene and safety, including the provision of basic necessities, in accordance with existing regulations and procedures.
It also urged the public to refrain from speculation and the dissemination of unverified information that could cause confusion and concern, advising them to refer to the department’s official channels for accurate information.
Earlier today, Lawyers for Liberty, in a statement, raised concerns over alleged water shortages and unsanitary conditions at Kajang Prison.
The concerns followed a complaint received last Monday from lawyers representing inmates involved in trials under the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (Sosma), which are held within the prison premises.
The complaints included limited water supply, insufficient drinking water, difficulties accessing toilets, dirty food trays and concerns over the hygiene of meals provided to inmates. — Bernama

Title: Apology on Threads but not in newspapers: Man faces contempt proceedings in Christy Ng defamation case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — A man ordered to pay fashion entrepreneur Christy Ng and her company RM180,000 in damages over defamatory social media posts is facing contempt of court proceedings after allegedly failing to publish apologies in newspapers as directed by the High Court.
The High Court in Kuala Lumpur has fixed Monday to hear a committal application filed by Ng and Christy Ng Sdn Bhd against J Vikneshvra Rau,
Berita Harian
reported.
The proceedings centre on Vikneshvra’s alleged failure to publish full-page, unconditional apologies in Malay- and English-language newspapers, despite having posted an apology on his Threads account in March.
According to a statement issued by law firm Foong Cheng Leong & Co, the dispute began with statements published through Vikneshvra’s Threads account, @archnionverse, on November 4 last year.
The post reportedly attracted at least 655,000 views, about 1,000 reposts and 1,800 shares.
On February 13, the High Court entered judgment in default of appearance against Vikneshvra after he failed to enter an appearance to defend the lawsuit.
The court barred him from publishing further defamatory statements and ordered him to issue public apologies in three newspapers and on his social media account.
Although Vikneshvra posted an apology on Threads on March 19, he allegedly failed to comply with the newspaper publication requirement, including in The Star and Harian Metro.
On September 15, the High Court granted Ng and her company permission to initiate committal proceedings against him for alleged contempt of court.
Committal proceedings allow a court to determine whether someone has committed contempt by failing to comply with its orders.
However, permission to bring the application does not mean Vikneshvra has been found guilty of contempt. The court must still consider the arguments and evidence presented by both sides before reaching a decision.
Ng and her company maintain that his continued failure to publish the required newspaper apologies amounts to non-compliance with the court’s order.
The latest proceedings follow an earlier High Court ruling on July 30, when Ng and her company were awarded RM180,000 in damages following an assessment.
Ng was awarded RM140,000, while her company received RM40,000.
Vikneshvra was also ordered to pay interest and RM10,000 in costs, alongside the requirement to publish apologies in three newspapers and on social media.
Ng and her company are represented by lawyers Foong Cheng Leong and Rachel Tan Li Ying of Foong Cheng Leong & Co.

Title: Fatal crash drivers could face asset seizure if compensation to victims unpaid, says Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Proposed amendments to federal road transport laws could empower courts to seize the assets of drivers convicted of fatal crashes if they fail to pay court-ordered compensation to victims’ families, Transport Minister Anthony Loke told Parliament today.
The government is currently drafting amendments to the Road Transport Act 1987 (Act 333) to establish a mandatory compensation mechanism for victims and next-of-kin affected by reckless driving and driving under the influence (DUI).
Replying during Question Time, Loke revealed that the ministry is exploring asset seizure alongside tougher secondary penalties, such as heavier fines or extended prison sentences to prevent convicted drivers from evading financial restitution.
“What happens if they are unable to pay that compensation? Under existing provisions in other acts, if they cannot afford to pay the compensation, there may be an additional fine or a heavier prison sentence imposed, on top of the original sentence,” the minister said.
“Secondly, we are also looking into whether the seizure of the offender’s assets can be carried out,” he added.
“However, I do not want to make any premature judgments because this matter is still under study as to what the best mechanism would be... the underlying spirit is indeed about finding a mechanism to ensure that the compensation can truly be paid to the heirs or families of the victims.”
The legal overhaul follows heightened public outcry over recurring fatal crashes caused by impaired drivers. Under current legislation, while offenders face imprisonment, heavy fines, and licence disqualifications, victims’ families are often forced to endure lengthy, costly civil proceedings to claim damages.
The proposed amendments under Act 333, according to the government, align with international legal principles and the Islamic concept of diyat, or financial compensation to the victim’s heirs.
The Cabinet approved the policy in principle earlier this year, and Loke stated that the amendment bill is expected to be tabled in Parliament in early 2027, following final policy formulation, legislative drafting by the Attorney General’s Chambers, and stakeholder engagements.

Title: Sultan Ibrahim attends day two of 273rd Conference of Rulers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today attended the second day of the 273rd Conference of Rulers meeting at Istana Negara here.
The meeting was chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah.
Also in attendance were the Raja of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Jamalullail; Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah; Sultan of Kedah, Al-Aminul Karim Sultan Sallehuddin Sultan Badlishah; and Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah.
Also present were the Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail; Crown Prince of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra; and Tunku Temenggong of Johor, Tunku Idris Iskandar Sultan Ibrahim.
The meeting was also attended by the four Governors, namely Tun Dr Mohd Ali Rustam of Melaka, Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar of Sarawak, Tun Musa Aman of Sabah and Tun Ramli Ngah Talib of Penang.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim also attended, together with menteri besar, chief ministers and Sarawak deputy premier. — Bernama
